title: Company-wide policies and processes: access, change, data, procurement, vendors, travel, templates
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel policies, and internal templates. It is intended for all employees and managers to ensure consistent compliance, security, and operational efficiency. Owners and escalation contacts are listed per section.

Table of contents
1. Access & permissions
2. Change management
3. Data management
4. Procurement & expenses
5. Vendor management
6. Travel policy
7. Internal templates and examples

1) Access & permissions

Purpose
- Ensure principle of least privilege (PoLP) across systems and cloud projects.
- Standardize onboarding and offboarding to reduce security risk.

Scope
- Applies to all Redwood systems: cloud accounts, production clusters, internal tools, GitHub, CI/CD, and third-party services.

Ownership
- Primary owner: Security & Compliance (owner_team: security).
- Operational owner: People Ops (onboarding/offboarding workflows).

Key policies
- Role-based access control (RBAC) is enforced for all services. No user may have permanent administrative access unless approved via the Executive Access process.
- Access reviews occur quarterly for production systems; team leads are responsible for attestation.
- Temporary elevation (break-glass) requires a JIRA ticket, approval from two approvers (team lead + security), and automatic expiry (max 8 hours).

Onboarding checklist (4 steps)
1. People Ops creates employee record and issues initial credentials.
2. Manager opens onboarding access request in Access JIRA with required roles.
3. Security reviews and approves in 48 hours (SLA).
4. Manager verifies access and completes a first-week attestation.

Offboarding checklist (mandatory immediate actions)
1. People Ops triggers offboarding in HR system.
2. Revoke cloud console, VPN, SSO, and GitHub access within 4 hours of termination notice.
3. If on-prem or device managed, schedule device wipe and return.

Access request template (use in Access JIRA)
- Requestor: full name and email
- Justification: business need and duration
- Systems/roles requested: list services and roles
- Approver: manager and security reviewer

Access review table (example)
| System | Review cadence | Owner | Acceptable deviation |
|--------|----------------|-------|----------------------|
| Production API cluster | Quarterly | Eng-SRE | < 2 admin accounts per service |
| GitHub org | Quarterly | Eng-Developer-Experience | Admins limited to staff+ |

Escalation and emergency access
- Security Pager (on-call) must be contacted for suspected compromise.
- Emergency privilege grant: documented ticket, 2 approvers, auto-revoke.

2) Change management

Purpose
- Reduce risk of outages and data loss by requiring standardized review, testing, and rollout for changes that affect production.

When to file a change request
- All changes to production infrastructure, model serving runtime, billing/configuration that can affect customers, or access permissions must have a Change Request (CR) in the Change Management board.

Change categories and approval matrix
- Standard (low risk): non-customer-facing config updates, routine updates. Approval: team lead.
- Significant (medium risk): runtime/config changes, schema migrations. Approval: engineering manager + SRE reviewer.
- Major (high risk): DB migrations, infra network changes, rollout of new model families. Approval: Eng Director + Security + Product.

Required fields for CR
- Title, owner, change type, impact, rollback plan, test plan, scheduled window, monitoring & success criteria, stakeholders, post-change validation steps.

Deployment windows and SLOs
- Normal change window: 09:00-17:00 UTC Mon-Fri. For high-risk changes use scheduled weekend windows and obtain Exec approval.
- Change review SLA: Standard changes: 48 hours; Significant: 72 hours; Major: 5 business days.

Review checklist (pre-deploy)
1. CR filed with complete required fields.
2. Unit/integration tests pass.
3. Canary with 1% traffic for 30 mins with health checks green.
4. Monitoring hooks and alerts configured.
5. Rollback validated in staging.

Rollback procedure (summary)
1. If post-deploy failures exceed threshold (see monitoring thresholds), trigger rollback.
2. Notify stakeholders via incident channel and update CR.
3. Postmortem required for significant/major rollbacks.

Monitoring thresholds (examples)
- Error rate increase > 1% absolute from baseline sustained for 10 minutes.
- p95 latency regression > 20% relative for 5 minutes.

3) Data management

Purpose
- Ensure data integrity, privacy, and compliance while enabling teams to use data for model evaluation and product development.

Data classification
- Confidential: customer PII, secrets, keys, identifiable logs.
- Internal: product metrics, staff information (non-sensitive).
- Public: marketing assets and docs marked for public release.

Data handling requirements
- Confidential data must be stored encrypted at rest and in transit, with KMS-backed keys. Access restricted to least-privileged roles.
- Anonymization/pseudonymization required prior to using production data in non-production environments.
- Backups: daily snapshots retained 30 days for non-critical, 90 days for critical systems; longer retention requires approval from Finance & Security.

Data retention and deletion
- Customer support logs: retain 180 days by default, extended retention requires approval.
- Model training corpora: retain per project policy; PII must be removed prior to storage.

Data breach procedure (high-level)
1. Immediately notify Security & Legal.
2. Triage and contain exposures within 4 hours.
3. Notify affected customers as required by contract and law.
4. Conduct root-cause analysis and publish internal incident review.

Data access request flow (example)
1. File Data Access Request (DAR) in the Data board with purpose and justification.
2. Data owner approves and sets access expiration.
3. Security & Data Governance validate encryption and handling.

4) Procurement & expenses

Purpose
- Standardize purchases, vendor selection, and expense reimbursement to control spend and ensure compliance.

Procurement thresholds
- Low (< $5k): Manager approval.
- Medium ($5k- $50k): Finance approval and two quotes if applicable.
- High (> $50k): Finance + VP or Exec approval and RFP preferred.

Procurement workflow (steps)
1. Initiator submits Purchase Request (PR) with justification, budget code, and business owner.
2. Procurement reviews, collects quotes if needed, and routes for approval.
3. Purchase Order (PO) issued; vendor onboarding checklist executed.
4. Finance records the spend and integrates into monthly forecasting.

Expense reimbursement policy (employee expenses)
- Use corporate card where possible. Personal card expenses require itemized receipts and submission within 30 days.
- Per diem: follow published country-specific rates (link to master table).
- Approval requires manager sign-off; expenses above $1,000 require Finance review.

Sample purchase order table
| Field | Required? | Notes |
|-------|-----------|-------|
| Vendor name | yes | Legal name for contract |
| Itemized list | yes | Attach quotes/invoices |
| Budget code | yes | Department cost center |
| Delivery/Service date | yes | Estimated ETA |

5) Vendor management

Purpose
- Ensure third-party risk is assessed and contractual controls are in place.

Vendor lifecycle
- Evaluate -> Onboard -> Monitor -> Offboard

Onboarding checklist (must be completed before PO/contract finalization)
- Security questionnaire completed and reviewed by Security.
- Contract with appropriate SLAs and data protection clauses signed by Legal.
- Vendor contact, escalation, and support details recorded.
- If vendor processes customer data, ensure DPIA or equivalent assessment is complete.

Performance and renewal
- Monitor vendor SLAs monthly; renewals > $25k escalate to Finance & Legal for terms review.
- Maintain scorecard for strategic vendors (availability, support responsiveness, cost variance).

Termination and offboarding
- Revoke vendor access, ensure data return/destruction per contract, and complete offboarding checklist.

6) Travel policy

Purpose
- Provide clear rules for business travel booking, expense eligibility, and approvals while controlling cost and risk.

Booking rules
- Use the corporate travel portal or preferred travel partner for flights and hotels.
- Economy class for flights < 6 hours, premium economy or business needs VP approval.

Approvals and pre-trip steps
1. Submit Travel Request with purpose, estimated cost, and approver.
2. Manager approves and Finance does a spot-check for trips > $3k.
3. Complete travel safety checklist for international travel (visas, vaccinations, local travel advisories).

Reimbursable expenses
- Itemized meals (receipts), lodging, ground transportation, reasonable internet fees.
- Non-reimbursable: leisure upgrades, fines, family costs unless pre-approved.

Emergency and duty-of-care
- People Ops and Security provide 24/7 duty-of-care contact for emergencies. Register travel in the People Ops travel registry before departure.

7) Internal templates and examples

Included templates (copy/paste into your JIRA/Confluence):
- Access Request (Access JIRA): Title, Requestor, Systems, Roles, Justification, Duration, Approvals.
- Change Request (Change board): Title, Owner, Type, Impact, Rollback, Monitoring, Stakeholders, Rollout Plan.
- Data Access Request (Data board): Project, Purpose, Data sets, Retention, Anonymization checklist, Approvals.
- Purchase Request template: Vendor, Items, Quotes, Budget code, Approvals, Delivery ETA.

Example: Change Request minimal template
- Title: "Canary: runtime-config v2 rollout"
- Owner: "SRE Team - Oncall"
- Impact: "Potential 5% latency change during canary"
- Rollback: "Revert config and redeploy previous image via deployment pipeline"
- Monitoring: "p95 latency, error rate, CPU/GPU utilization"

Contacts and escalation list
- People Ops: people-ops@redwood.ai (onboarding/offboarding)
- Security & Compliance: security@redwood.ai (access reviews, vendor security)
- Finance & Procurement: procurement@redwood.ai (POs, vendor contracts)
- Eng-SRE on-call: see internal roster (linked in eng-sre runbooks)

Governance, review cadence, and amendments
- This document is reviewed at least annually by People Ops, Security, and Finance. Significant regulatory changes or incidents may trigger an immediate review.
- Any team may propose amendments via a PR in the Policies board; approvers include owners listed above.
